description: Bug #2 — QMetry fetch must resolve EVERY candidate key to its own QMetry project AND folder, export every distinct folder, and MERGE all parsed test cases into one dict de-duped by QMetry TC key, instead of resolving a single project+folder and exporting only the first. Also fix plumbing so enrich_scenarios_with_qmetry receives BOTH jira.subtasks AND jira.links (plus the epic children captured by FEAT-001). Depends on FEAT-001 for the full related-key set. All downstream matching/eligibility stays unchanged and now operates over the merged set.
steps: In C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\TestSuiteGenerator\.worktrees\qmetry-multi-link\modules\qmetry_steps_source.py, add a per-key folder resolver (e.g. _resolve_folders_for_keys(client, project_id, candidate_keys, log)) that applies the existing tiered matching from _resolve_folder_id (PASS 1 full-key containment, PASS 2 truncated issue-number with digit boundary, line 567) PER key and collects EACH key's matched folder id into an ordered, de-duplicated list — never stopping at the first match. Keep _resolve_folder_id intact for the single-key case.

Rework fetch_authored_steps (def line 625) to iterate ALL valid candidate keys (every subtask + every epic-child + every link + the feature key). For each key: resolve its QMetry project via resolve_project_dynamic (fallback resolve_project_id), construct the QMetryRestClient for THAT project, resolve its folder(s) via the new per-key resolver (constrained to that key so one key's folder cannot match another key's cases), export each distinct (project_id, folder_id) exactly once, parse via parse_qmetry_xlsx + _apply_packed_rule, and MERGE parsed TCs into one dict keyed by TC key; later keys must NOT overwrite a TC key already present (de-dup by QMetry TC key). Preserve graceful skip (return {}) when no key resolves, and fail-loud QMetryFetchError on export/parse failure. Optionally add fetch_authored_steps_multi and have fetch_authored_steps delegate so the single-key signature/behavior stays backward compatible for existing tests.

Change _FOLDER_MEMO (line 512) to be keyed per (project_id, candidate_key) instead of (project_id, feature_key); update the memo read/write currently at lines 657-662 accordingly. Keep the per-(project_id, folder_id) _EXPORT_CACHE (line 511) and the 6h disk cache unchanged.

In enrich_scenarios_with_qmetry (def line 1063), build the candidate key list from jira.subtasks AND jira.links/linked_issues (epic children arrive inside jira.subtasks from FEAT-001). Pass the union to fetch_authored_steps and pass _valid_keys(union) as validated_keys to attach_steps_to_scenarios (line 855). Do not truncate; include every key. Apply the same union at both enrich call sites in modules/data_first_engine.py (main path ~line 325 and CR path ~line 1120) if they pre-compute keys.

Leave the matcher and gates unchanged (value-pair tier-1, 0.60 similarity tier-2, Tier-3 ADD-AS-NEW-TC relevance gate, _story_linkage_eligible, Chalk-first ordering, grounding, banned-phrase backstop); they now operate over the merged multi-folder dict. _story_linkage_eligible already accepts a TC whose linkages contain ANY validated key.

Extend tests/test_qmetry_steps_source.py (reuse _FakeClient, _stub_project_index, fixture-xlsx helpers; clear qss._EXPORT_CACHE, qss._FOLDER_MEMO, and set qss._PROJECT_INDEX=None at test start) with: (a) multi-project merge — keys spanning two QMetry projects/folders (e.g. NSLNM-784 -> NSLNM folder, MWTGNBOP-5791/5792 -> MWTGNBOP folder) merge every folder's TCs into one dict de-duped by TC key; (b) single-key feature -> exactly one folder resolved+exported, result identical to pre-change (no behavior change); (c) eligibility — a TC whose Story Linkages contain ANY validated linked key (e.g. NSLNM-784) is eligible and attached/added, not dropped.
acceptance_criteria: fetch_authored_steps resolves and exports EVERY candidate key's own project+folder and merges all parsed TCs into one dict de-duped by QMetry TC key.
A single-key feature resolves exactly one folder and exports once, with result byte-for-byte equal to the pre-change behavior.
enrich_scenarios_with_qmetry receives both jira.subtasks and jira.links plus the epic children.
A TC story-linked to ANY validated linked key is eligible and kept.

New multi-project merge / single-key / eligibility tests pass; all existing QMetry tests stay green; project-agnostic resolver, fail-loud QMetrySessionError, session guard, CR path hook, grounding and no-garbage guarantees intact.
verification: C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_qmetry_steps_source.py tests/test_cr_qmetry_supplement.py -q  (from the worktree root) — passes
C:\Users\P3314665\Documents\mcp-jira-server\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q -m "not slow"  (from the worktree root) — all pass
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (modules/qmetry_steps_source.py + tests/test_qmetry_steps_source.py only; no other source touched). (1) _resolve_folders_for_keys(client, project_id, candidate_keys, log) added — resolves EACH key INDEPENDENTLY via the intact single-key _resolve_folder_id([key]) (so one key's number can never match another key's folder), collecting an ordered, de-duped list of folder ids; never stops at the first match. Memoized per (project_id, candidate_key). (2) _resolve_folder_id is UNCHANGED (single-key tiered PASS1 full-key / PASS2 truncated-number). (3) New helper _export_and_parse_folder(client, project_id, folder_id, log) carries the former single-folder export/parse + run-cache + 6h disk-cache + fail-loud QMetryFetchError logic, now called once per distinct folder. (4) fetch_authored_steps reworked: resolves EVERY candidate key's folder within its project and MERGES all folders' parsed TCs into one dict de-duped by QMetry TC key (a TC key already present is NOT overwritten by a later folder). A single-key feature resolves exactly one folder and exports once -> byte-identical to pre-change. (5) New fetch_authored_steps_multi(project_keys, feature_key, cookies, log): takes an ORDERED {project_id: [keys]} map, calls fetch_authored_steps per project, and merges the per-project dicts de-duped by TC key (earlier project wins). (6) _FOLDER_MEMO re-keyed per (project_id, candidate_key) (comment + usage). _EXPORT_CACHE stays per (project_id, folder_id); 6h disk cache unchanged. (7) enrich_scenarios_with_qmetry now builds the related-key set from jira.subtasks (carrying FEAT-001 epic children) AND jira.linked_issues, resolves EACH key to its OWN QMetry project (dynamic /projects first, static QMETRY_PROJECT_MAP fallback), GROUPS keys by project preserving first-seen order, calls fetch_authored_steps_multi, and passes _valid_keys(related_keys) (subtasks+links union) as validated_keys to attach_steps_to_scenarios. cookies still load FIRST (fail-loud QMetrySessionError preserved). When no key maps to any project it skips gracefully (returns 0). (8) data_first_engine.py was NOT edited: both enrich call sites (main ~line 325, CR ~line 1120) call enrich_scenarios_with_qmetry(scenarios, jira, options, log) and do NOT pre-compute keys, so the union now lives entirely inside enrich; no call-site change was needed (step 4's 'if they pre-compute keys' did not apply). (9) Matcher/gates (value-pair tier-1, 0.60 similarity tier-2, Tier-3 relevance gate, _story_linkage_eligible accepting ANY validated key, Chalk-first ordering, grounding, banned-phrase backstop) all UNCHANGED — they now operate over the merged multi-folder dict.

TESTS ADDED (tests/test_qmetry_steps_source.py, hermetic; clear qss._EXPORT_CACHE/_FOLDER_MEMO and set _PROJECT_INDEX=None; disk cache redirected to a temp dir): (a) test_multi_project_merge — keys across NSLNM (link NSLNM-784) + MWTGNBOP (subtasks 5791/5792) projects/folders merge into one dict, distinct TCs from BOTH present, a shared TC key appears once keeping the FIRST-seen (subtask/NBOP) variant; (b) test_single_key_feature_one_folder_unchanged — exactly one folder resolved + one export, result identical to pre-change; (c) test_eligibility_any_validated_linked_key — a TC story-linked ONLY to a validated LINKED key (NSLNM-784 arriving via jira.linked_issues, no subtasks) is eligible and added as a NEW TC.

VERIFICATION: tests/test_qmetry_steps_source.py + tests/test_cr_qmetry_supplement.py -> 34 passed. Full fast suite (-m 'not slow', run with --continue-on-collection-errors) -> 420 passed, 3 skipped. PRE-EXISTING, NOT caused by this change (identical to FEAT-001's recorded baseline): 26 collection errors 'No module named shared' (nested worktree breaks jira_fetcher's relative _SHARED_PATH; without --continue-on-collection-errors pytest aborts before running) and 2 cache-data failures (test_ac_gate::test_4349_role_list_survives, test_near_dup_pruning::test_4136_recovers_its_jira_and_subtask_coverage) from empty subtasks in the worktree's tsg_cache.db. Neither failing test touches qmetry_steps_source.

FOR CONVERGENCE: FEAT-002 is self-contained in modules/qmetry_steps_source.py (committed on fix/qmetry-multi-link). It depends on FEAT-001's capture of epic children into jira.subtasks (and FEAT-001's shared/jira_fetcher/database edits, which — per FEAT-001's findings — live in the SEPARATE monorepo repo on branch feature/tsg-v9-dedup-fixes, NOT on fix/qmetry-multi-link). At runtime jira.subtasks + jira.linked_issues now feed the multi-project/multi-folder QMetry merge, so MWTGPROV-4575 pulls both MWTGNBOP subtask cases AND the NSLNM-784 linked cases. Run full-suite verification with --continue-on-collection-errors (or make 'shared' importable) because the 26 pre-existing collection errors otherwise abort the run before tests execute.
